# Incident Report: FedEx-Themed Phishing → JS Dropper → Encrypted C2 Beacon

## Victim Host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.8.15.133** |
| MAC | **00:1c:bf:03:54:82** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-H8ALZBV** (AD domain LAFONTAINEBLEU, DC WIN-JEGJIX7Q9RS.lafontainebleu.org) |
| Logged-in user | **plucero** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString, frames in stream from 10.8.15.133/10.8.15.4) |

## Malware Family
**Attribution: behavioral**, with one signature-grade artifact.

The delivery chain matches a JS-dropper pattern (oversized JavaScript padded with scraped document text to inflate file size, malicious logic hidden inside `/*...*/` comments) consistent with GootLoader-style loaders. The dropped second-stage payload is a 64-bit DLL whose embedded PDB debug path reads:

```
E:\work\ooooooops\181\knock_v1.1.8\knock\bin64\knock.pdb
```

This gives a **signature-confirmed internal build identity of "Knock" (v1.1.8)** for the second-stage payload itself (this string is not a publicly-recognized commodity family name I can independently verify without external lookup, which was out of scope). The initial-access mechanism (fake invoice phishing → oversized JS in ZIP → BITS-delivered DLL → encrypted HTTP POST beacon with a legacy IE6 user-agent) is assessed **behaviorally** as a loader/backdoor infection chain.

## Infection Chain (evidence-grounded)
1. **Phishing lure**: Host resolved and repeatedly queried `quote.checkfedexexp.com` and `business.checkfedexexp.com` (frames 6200-6413, 9026-9027), resolving to `104.21.55.70` / `172.67.170.159` (Cloudflare-fronted).
2. **Payload download**: `GET /managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215` to host `quote.checkfedexexp.com` (frame 6418) returned `application/octet-stream` (frame 8659) — a ZIP archive containing:
   - **`Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js`** — 6,990,020 bytes, mostly garbage text (climate reports, MPI standard docs, browser-privacy wiki pages) padding, with executable statements (e.g. `WScript.Sleep(10000);`) hidden inline. Contains one live reference to `https://business.checkfedexexp.com/data-privacy?...`.
3. **Second-stage fetch via BITS**: `Microsoft BITS/7.8` user-agent performed `HEAD`/`GET /data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` to **72.5.43.29** (frames 10611, 10614, tcp.stream 134) → 159,232-byte **PE32+ x86-64 DLL** (internal name `release.dll`, PDB `knock.pdb`).
4. **C2 beaconing**: Starting ~frame 11028, the host opened a new TCP connection roughly every 10-15 seconds to **72.5.43.29:80**, sending `GET /` or `POST /` with a legacy `Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)` user-agent, a large base64 blob in the `Cookie:` header, and (on POST) an encrypted binary body (e.g. `Content-Length: 305148` on stream 143). Server responded `HTTP/1.1 400` each time. This pattern repeated **306 times** across the remainder of the capture (last observed ~frame 18186), consistent with active C2 check-in/exfiltration.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoints**
- `72.5.43.29:80` (persistent encrypted-beacon C2, 306+ requests)

**Domains**
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com`
- `business.checkfedexexp.com`

**URLs**
- `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215` (ZIP payload)
- `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` (second-stage DLL)
- `https://business.checkfedexexp.com/data-privacy?zj=ZzqRKxVRQ&pOd=GEokiOXFwH&sourcedp=tQMQJlIo&Tfocontent` (referenced inside the JS dropper)

**Files / hashes**
| File | SHA256 |
|---|---|
| ZIP payload (`managements?...`) | `798563fcf7600f7ef1a35996291a9dfb5f9902733404dd499e2e736ea1dc6fc5` |
| `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` | `dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c` |
| `0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` (PE64 DLL, PDB `knock.pdb` v1.1.8) | `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6` |

## Benign Context (not IOCs)
Traffic to Microsoft/Windows Update, Bing/MSN, Adobe (`acroipm2.adobe.com`), Akamai/Edgekey CDN ranges (23.220.x, 23.53.x, 23.43.x), OCSP (`oneocsp.microsoft.com`), and normal AD/Kerberos/LDAP/DHCP/NBNS traffic to the domain controller (10.8.15.4) is standard workstation/domain noise, not malicious.

## Summary
Windows workstation DESKTOP-H8ALZBV (10.8.15.133, MAC 00:1c:bf:03:54:82), logged in as user **plucero** on domain LAFONTAINEBLEU, visited a FedEx-themed phishing site (`quote.checkfedexexp.com` / `business.checkfedexexp.com`) and downloaded a ZIP containing a heavily obfuscated, oversized JavaScript dropper (`Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js`). That dropper used BITS to pull a second-stage 64-bit DLL (internal build "Knock" v1.1.8, per its PDB path) from `72.5.43.29`, which then established persistent encrypted HTTP-based C2 communication to the same IP on port 80, using a spoofed legacy Internet Explorer user-agent, for the remainder of the capture.
